queue.title: Add delete functionality to Todo data model
queue.description:
Implement the core data layer functionality to remove todo items from storage. This foundational capability will support both ID-based and index-based deletion methods.

**Technical Requirements:**
- Add a `delete_todo()` method to the todo storage layer
- Support deletion by unique ID (primary method)
- Support deletion by index position (for user convenience)
- Handle edge cases: invalid IDs, out-of-bounds indices, empty lists
- Return appropriate success/error status
- Ensure data persistence after deletion

**Implementation Notes:**
- If using file-based storage, ensure atomic writes
- Maintain data integrity during deletion operations
- Consider adding soft delete capability for future undo functionality

queue.title: Implement 'delete' command with ID support
queue.description:
Create a command-line interface for deleting todo items by their unique ID. This provides the primary method for users to remove specific items from their todo list.

**User Interface:**
- Command format: `todo delete <id>`
- Display confirmation message with item details before deletion
- Show success/error messages with clear feedback
- Handle invalid or non-existent IDs gracefully

**Example Usage:**
```
$ todo delete 123
Delete todo: "Buy groceries" (completed: false)? [y/N] y
Todo item deleted successfully.

$ todo delete 999
Error: Todo item with ID 999 not found.
```

**Dependencies:**
- Requires completed delete functionality in data model

queue.title: Add delete by index number support
queue.description:
Extend the delete functionality to support deletion by index number (position in list). This provides an alternative, more intuitive way for users to delete items when working with numbered todo lists.

**User Interface:**
- Command format: `todo delete #<index>` or `todo delete <index>` (if index is clearly numeric)
- Index should match the numbers shown in `todo list` output
- Support 1-based indexing (matching list display)
- Include same confirmation flow as ID-based deletion

**Example Usage:**
```
$ todo list
1. [ID: 123] Buy groceries
2. [ID: 456] Walk the dog

$ todo delete #2
Delete todo: "Walk the dog" (completed: false)? [y/N] y
Todo item deleted successfully.

$ todo delete 5
Error: Todo item at index 5 not found. You have 1 items.
```

**Dependencies:**
- Requires completed delete functionality in data model
- Should integrate with existing delete command interface

queue.title: Add bulk delete functionality
queue.description:
Enable users to delete multiple todo items in a single operation. This improves efficiency when cleaning up completed tasks or removing multiple obsolete items.

**User Interface Options:**
1. `todo delete --all-completed` - Delete all completed items
2. `todo delete <id1> <id2> <id3>` - Delete multiple specific items
3. `todo delete #<index1> #<index2>` - Delete by multiple indices

**Example Usage:**
```
$ todo delete --all-completed
Delete 3 completed todo items? [y/N] y
Deleted 3 completed items successfully.

$ todo delete 123 456 789
Delete 3 todo items:
- "Buy groceries"
- "Walk dog"  
- "Call mom"
[y/N] y
Deleted 3 items successfully.
```

**Dependencies:**
- Requires basic delete functionality (ID and index)
- Should reuse confirmation patterns from single delete

queue.title: Add force delete option (skip confirmation)
queue.description:
Provide a way for power users to bypass the confirmation prompt when deleting todo items. This improves workflow efficiency for users who want to script deletions or perform bulk operations.

**User Interface:**
- Add `--force` or `-f` flag to delete commands
- Works with single, multiple, and bulk delete operations
- Include warning in help text about data loss risk

**Example Usage:**
```
$ todo delete 123 --force
Todo item deleted successfully.

$ todo delete --all-completed --force
Deleted 3 completed items successfully.

$ todo delete #1 #2 #3 -f
Deleted 3 items successfully.
```

**Safety Considerations:**
- Document the risk in help text
- Consider adding a global confirmation setting for future
- Ensure this works consistently across all delete variants

**Dependencies:**
- Requires all other delete functionality to be implemented first
